steps.text: Preheat oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Grease and flour a 9x13-inch jelly roll pan or line with parchment paper.
Combine flour, sugar, baking soda, and pumpkin pie spice in a large bowl. Stir in pumpkin puree, eggs, and lemon juice until just blended. Spread mixture evenly into prepared pan.
Bake in the preheated oven until cake springs back when lightly touched, about 15 minutes.

Lay a damp linen towel on the counter, sprinkle it with confectioners' sugar, and turn the cake onto the towel. Remove parchment paper if you used it. Carefully roll the towel up lengthwise (starting at the narrow end) with the warm cake in it. Place the cake-in-towel on a cooling rack and let it cool completely, about 1 to 2 hours.
To make the icing: Blend cream cheese, butter, vanilla, and sugar in a medium bowl with a wooden spoon or electric mixer. Chill icing until cake has cooled.
Unroll cooled cake and spread icing onto it. Immediately re-roll (not in the towel this time), and wrap it with plastic wrap. Chill the cake to set before slicing.

raw_recipe.headline: Granny Kat's Pumpkin Roll
raw_recipe.description: A sweetly spicy, pumpkin-flavored cake is spread with a silky rich cream cheese filling and rolled up like a pinwheel for a crowd-pleasing dessert.
raw_recipe.name: Granny Kat's Pumpkin Roll

review.reviewBody: I had fun making this. Had no problems whatsoever with the cake sticking to the pan or cracking. Here is what I did. I cut a piece of parchment paper to fit my pan then sprayed the edges of the pan with cooking spray. I allowed the cake to cool about 20 minutes then I lifted it out of the pan with parchment paper stuck to the bottom of it and flipped it (carefully) on to another piece of parchment paper with a generous amount of powdered sugar sprinkled on it. Then I just peeled the parchment off the bottom of the roll, spread on icing, sprinkled some finely chopped walnuts on top of icing and re-rolled the cake. Wrapped it up on a piece of heavy duty foil and put it freezer for about 45 minutes to set up. Then moved to fridge. Just fantastic. It's a beautiful presentation and the taste is incredible. If you are hesitating to try because it looks difficult you should definitely try it!

This was a disaster when I tried to roll it. My icing popped out so that I could not roll it tightly. Using less icing may help, and if I ever try this again, I will chill the icing until it is fairly firm and allow the cake to cool longer. Four stars for taste, negative one star for being a pain....**Update- 2nd attempt: I used wax paper on the pan, then another sheet on the inside when I rolled it. This prevented it from sticking to the towel. Greasing it would be good too. I didn't soften the c. cheese as much and chilled it while the cake cooled. This made it much easier to spread w/out gushing out. Came out almost as good looking as the pics-- I'll keep trying! Tastes awesome.

This cake tastes amazing! I recommend a couple changes to the recipe though.

My mom and I made two versions of this cake - one exactly following this recipe and one with a pumpkin spice version of the cream cheese frosting in the middle. We preferred the pumpkin spice cream cheese because it was easier to spread on the cake, and it didn't feel as heavy in our stomachs after eating it. To make the pumpkin spice cream cheese, we added 1/4 cup of pumpkin puree, 1.5 teaspoons of cinnamon, and a little less than 1/2 teaspoon of nutmeg to this cream cheese recipe.

It was really difficult to get the cake off the cookie sheet, so I highly recommend using a piece of aluminum foil. Grease and flour the aluminum foil, and bake as the directions say. This makes it easy to peel the aluminum foil off the cake after you flip it onto the towel, rather than trying to peel the cake off the cookie sheet.

We had some issues with the cake breaking as we tried to roll it, but we didn't care too much since we were the only ones eating it.
Beat the eggs for 5 minutes first to incorporate more air. Very good. I used 2 teaspoons cinnamon and 1/4 teaspoon nutmeg since I didn't have pumpkin pie spice.

So easy and delish!! I used a cookie sheet and greased it with crisco and then coated in flour. Cake didn’t stick at all! Then I used a silicone cookie rolling mat covered in confection sugar instead of a damp towel. It all came out perfect! I’m so proud of the final result and taste!!

This recipe has already become a family favorite. I used 3 tsp of pumpkin spice instead so it has more flavor. I also bake the cake for closer to 18-20 minutes. With my oven, 15 minutes left the cake gooey in the middle. I also turn the baked cake out onto plain parchment paper without sugar. When I tried turning it out onto a damp towel with powdered sugar, the cake absorbed the sugar and became too sticky on the outside. To decorate, I melt white chocolate with coconut oil and drizzle it onto the finished roll in swirls and circles. It makes for a beautiful finish.

Very good, very easy! I cut the sugar in the cake to 2/3 cup, &I double the frosting ingredients and make 3 cake rolls! I think that is the perfect amount, to the thickness of the cake roll! Also, I reuse the parchment paper just respray it each time!

I had never made a pumpkin roll so I started reading the reviews about this recipe before making mine. I was hoping to learn from other bakers what they changed, if anything. After making mine, the one suggestion I will follow when making my next is...use wax paper when rolling cake before cooling. I used a linen towel, made sure it was slightly damp & used a generous amount of confectionery sugar. It still stuck to the towel. It didn't ruin my cake but I'm going to try wax paper instead. I also put the cream cheese spread in the fridge while the cake was cooling (another great suggestion). Other than that, it turned out fantastic. Thank you to all the bakers that left their reviews.

I have been making this for at least 30 years it is very easy to make. if you have problems with the cake cracking make sure when you roll in the towel the towel is sprinkled generously with powdered sugar, and you make sure it cools completely at least 2 hours before you attempt to unroll and fill. also make sure you are using the correct size pan to bake the cake in if the cake is too thick it will crack. the recipe can easily be doubled to make two cakes and use the entire can of pumpkin. I like to chill my cake over night prior tofilling when done I double wrap in foil to freeze this cake freezes very well and I usually make the first week of November for Thanksgiving and I give it as gift to fire station and few friends. take it out of the freezer about an hour before serving. My family actually loves it frozen the filling tastes like ice cream

Loved it! I used a 15x10x1 inch pan lined with parchment paper. The parchment definitely aided in the rolling.

I also eyeballed the spices- cinnamon, fresh nutmeg, ginger, and a pinch of cloves.

this is a great recipe!! Only missing instruction is to bake in 11×15 cookie sheet and line it with parchment or Silpat. Dont skip the step of ring the,warm cake in a towel. this is very important!! also don't skip the lemon juice. this isn't for flavor but to react with the baking soda, giving you a nice light sponge. I have made hundreds of rolled cakes as a caterer and have never had one crack...ever! The towel is so important for siccess!!! I saw someone said that they rolled it in parchment, which I think could cause the heat to get trapped. you want it to cool evenly in the rolled position.

I have made it several times! Always delicious! A little tricky rolling/unrolling to make it look perfect, but great recipe! I made it in a 10"x15" pan so it was a little thinner-this made it easier to roll without cracking. I also let it completely cool, and chilled my cream cheese prior to spreading on the pumpkin roll!
I made one of these for Thanksgiving and everyone absolutely loved it. They loved it so much, I am making 4 more

This recipe is great and a definite favorite dessert for my family at Thanksgiving. It takes a bit of effort to get it done correctly but if you nail it 😙🤌. It's been added to the yearly dessert must-haves for sure.

Can't believe I made this ! Delicious ! I'm a new baker, wasn't too hard. Let cake cool completely and let chilled icing warm up to room temp. I would use parchment in addition to towel. Nicer texture on cake by not sticking to towel. Will try again!
I have been making this for YEARS and everyone that has tried it begs me to make it more often. At one point for Thanksgiving alone I had to make 8!!!
amazing just the wat it is!

The first time I tried this recipe was in a 9x13 pan, and the cake cracked when I went to unroll it after cooling for 1 hour in the fridge. The second time I made the cake on a cookie sheet and let the cake cool for 2 hours at room temperature in a damp tea towel, and it rolled/ unrolled perfectly. I think the thinner cake layer helped with not cracking, as well as handling the cake VERY gently when unrolling. I made the filling and added a 1/4 cup of pumpkin, 1/2 teaspoon cinnamon, and 1/8 teaspoon of nutmeg. It made the filling much more spreadable and delicious! Brought this in for a halloween potluck and it was a hit. I'm thinking about making this recipe for Thanksgiving this year instead of a pie!

I loved this recipe! My sheet cake cracked a little but that's cause of my mistakes ( putting it in the fridge too long) But it tasted great! The only things are the cake was rubbery and the cream cheese was rly hard to make! But great overall!

I get asked to make this year after year. I do use a little less powdered sugar in the filling (3/4 instead of 1 c). Tips: use a true jelly roll pan - 10x15, not a 9x13. Line the bottom of your pan with parchment paper before greasing/flouring the sides and bottom.
